requirements.req_text: Do the following: (a) Explain to your counselor the hazards you are most likely to encounter while using leatherwork tools and materials, and what you should do to anticipate, help prevent, mitigate, or lessen these hazards. (b) Show that you know first aid for injuries or illnesses that could occur while working with leather, including minor cuts and scratches, puncture wounds, ingested poisoning, and reactions from exposure to chemicals such as dyes, cements, and finishes used in leatherworking.

Core Standard 1 (Req 1): Do the following: (a) Explain to your counselor the hazards you are most likely to encounter while using leatherwork tools and materials, and what you should do to anticipate, help prevent, mitigate, or lessen these hazards.

Execute & Document: Perform the demonstrate task methodically with your patrol buddy and log specific observations in your Leatherwork Workbook.
Verify With Counselor: Present your completed work, demonstrate proficiency, and answer Socratic check-for-understanding questions for Blue Card sign-off.

requirements.req_text: Do ONE of the following: (a) Learn about the commercial tanning process. Report about it to your counselor. (b) Tan the skin of a small animal. Describe the safety precautions you will take and the tanning method that you used. (c) Recondition or show that you can take proper care of your shoes, a baseball glove, a saddle, furniture, or other articles of leather. Discuss with your counselor the advantages or disadvantages of leather vs. synthetic materials. (d) Visit a leather-related business. This could be a leathercraft supply company, a tannery, a leather goods or shoe factory, or a saddle shop. Report on your visit to your counselor.

pamphlet_excerpts: Leatherwork Sub-Req 5a: Learn about the commercial tanning process. Report about it to your counselor.
Leatherwork Sub-Req 5b: Tan the skin of a small animal. Describe the safety precautions you will take and the tanning method that you used.
Leatherwork Sub-Req 5c: Recondition or show that you can take proper care of your shoes, a baseball glove, a saddle, furniture, or other articles of leather. Discuss.
Leatherwork Sub-Req 5d: Visit a leather-related business. This could be a leathercraft supply company, a tannery, a leather goods or shoe factory, or a saddle shop. Report.
step_by_step_procedure: Prepare & Inspect (Req 5): Review the official Leatherwork requirement standard and verify all required tools, reference tables, and safety gear.
Analyze Core Principles: Identify the primary concepts, definitions, and cause-and-effect relationships governing (a) Learn about the commercial tanning process. Report.
Execute & Document: Perform the explain task methodically with your patrol buddy and log specific observations in your Leatherwork Workbook.
Verify With Counselor: Present your completed work, demonstrate proficiency, and answer Socratic check-for-understanding questions for Blue Card sign-off.
gear_checklist: Official Leatherwork Merit Badge Pamphlet & Fillable Scout Workbook (open to Req 5)
Activity-Specific Tools, Reference Charts & Measuring Instruments for Leatherwork Req 5
Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) & First-Aid Readiness Kit per BSA Guide to Safe Scouting
Signed Blue Card (Application for Merit Badge #34124) or Scoutbook Digital Record

left_points: Skips pre-task hazard scan and relies on guesswork during Requirement 5.
Provides vague, one-word workbook notes without measurable field evidence.
Rushes past buddy verification and cannot explain why each step matters.
right_points: Completes a structured safety and equipment check before starting Requirement 5.
Records concrete measurements, examples, and citations from Official BSA Leatherwork Pamphlet, pp. 28-33.
Demonstrates mastery using the BSA EDGE method (Explain, Demonstrate, Guide, Enable).
